sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface FLAG signal detected by flow cytometry on non-permeabilized HUVEC, confirming GPI-anchored surface display. Complement-inhibitory function of CD59 NOT MEASURED in this clip.
sites.rationale: CD59 is a GPI-anchored protein with no TM domain; the entire mature sequence (residues 26–128) is extracellular. The paper describes a 'C-terminus of full-length CD59' FLAG tag with confirmed surface display, and the only extracellular C-terminus in the canonical sequence is after residue 128 (P). No specific residue is named in the clip, so the junction is topology-derived from the single available C-terminal landmark. The TM-distance constraint does not apply as there is no TM helix. Full-length CD59-FLAG construct expressed in HUVEC; non-permeabilized staining with anti-FLAG(M1)-DL488 by flow cytometry confirmed surface display of the GPI-anchored tagged protein.

sources.claim: B) HUVEC were co‐transfected with either mCerulean‐C1 empty vector (control), mCerulean‐GDPD5 or mCerulean‐GDPD5‐H233A and the respective FLAG‐tagged GPI‐AP target (CD59‐FLAG, NT5E‐FLAG or TFPI‐FLAG). 24 h post transfection, cells were detached, fixed and stained for the surface FLAG signal using anti‐FLAG(M1)‐DL488 antibodies.

literature_notes: CD59 (P13987) is a GPI-anchored complement regulatory protein. The sole ledger line (L1) reports a C-terminal FLAG tag on full-length CD59 with surface display confirmed by non-permeabilized flow cytometry. No residue number is stated, so the position is topology-derived as insert_after_residue=128 (the last residue P of the canonical 128-aa sequence). The GPI signal peptide (approximately residues 78–128 in full-length numbering) is normally cleaved and replaced by the GPI anchor; the confirmed surface display of the FLAG tag indicates the GPI-anchoring machinery remained functional in this construct, consistent with published strategies that append short tags C-terminal to the mature domain or within the GPI signal. No N-terminal internal or other loop insertions are supported by the ledger. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions were reported.
